title: Pseudo-bulk generation strategies for phenotype-guided single-cell benchmarking
text: Tip specific setting — approximately 20,000 single cells 8 barcoded organoids, four successful four failed differentiation outcomes — avoid relying single pseudo-bulk design. robust benchmark use three nested levels: Observed organoid pseudo-bulk \[ Y_b=\sum_{c:b(c)=b}x_c \] gives \(8\) realistic pseudo-bulk samples. Organoid-preserving bootstraps \[ Y_{br}^{\mathrm{boot}}=\sum_{c\\mathcal{C}_{br}}x_c, \qquad \mathcal{C}_{br}\subseteq\{c:b(c)=b\} \] gives technical replicates preserving barcode structure. Phenotype-stratified custom-composition simulations \[ Y_i=\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{c\\mathcal{C}_{ik}}x_c, \qquad (N_{i1},\ldots,N_{iK})\sim\mathrm{Multinomial}(N_i,\pi_i) \] creates controlled success/failure pseudo-bulk cohorts known ground truth.

title: Pseudo-bulk generation strategies for phenotype-guided single-cell benchmarking
text: single-cell expression vectors independent Gaussian, \[ x_c\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma), \] aggregation simple: \[ Y_i=\sum_{c=1}^{N_i}x_c \sim \mathcal{N}(N_i\mu,N_i\Sigma). \] cells share organoid-level programs, \[ \mathrm{Cov}(x_c,x_{c'})=C \quad (c\neq c'), \] \[ \mathrm{Var}(Y_i) = N_i\Sigma + N_i(N_i-1)C. \] \(N_i(N_i-1)C\) term means shared biological programs can dominate pseudo-bulk variance. Therefore, naïve aggregation can overstate biological signal many bootstraps reuse organoids. log-normal single-cell models, \[ x_c=\exp(z_c),\qquad z_c\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\Sigma), \] sum \[ Y_i=\sum_c x_c \] exactly log-normal. Moment-matching Gaussian CLT approximations may used, sparse precision matrix inferred single-cell level generally preserved aggregation.
